questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context

questions.question_text:
Some people believe that “what gets measured, improves”. Some others believe
that “what gets measured, gets gamed”. One possible reason for the difference in
the beliefs is the work culture in organizations. In organizations with good work
culture, metrics help improve outcomes. However, the same metrics are
counterproductive in organizations with poor work culture.
Which one of the following is the CORRECT logical inference based on the
information in the above passage?

options.A: Metrics are useful in organizations with poor work culture
options.B: Metrics are useful in organizations with good work culture
options.C: Metrics are always counterproductive in organizations with good work culture
options.D: Metrics are never useful in organizations with good work culture

questions.explaination: The passage explicitly notes that "In organizations with good work culture, metrics help improve outcomes." This directly implies that metrics are useful in organizations with good work culture.

questions.question_text: We reached the station late, and _______ missed the train.
questions.subtopic: Basic English grammar: tenses, articles, adjectives, prepositions, conjunctions, verb-noun agreement
questions.explaination: The adverb 'nearly' means 'almost' and correctly modifies the past-tense verb 'missed'. 'Near' is an adjective/preposition, while 'utterly' and 'mostly' do not fit the intended semantic meaning of narrowly missing a train.
questions.question_text_latex: We reached the station late, and \_\_\_\_\_\_\_ missed the train.

questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context
questions.explaination: 'Often' and 'Frequently' are direct synonyms. 'Kind' can be a noun meaning 'Type' (category) or an adjective meaning benevolent/caring. Because of multiple ambiguous interpretations of 'Kind', GATE awarded Marks to All (MTA) for this question.

questions.question_text:
The country of Zombieland is in distress since more than 75% of its working
population is suffering from serious health issues. Studies conducted by competent
health experts concluded that a complete lack of physical exercise among its
working population was one of the leading causes of their health issues. As one of
the measures to address the problem, the Government of Zombieland has decided
to provide monetary incentives to those who ride bicycles to work.

Based only on the information provided above, which one of the following
statements can be logically inferred with certainty?

options.A: All the working population of Zombieland will henceforth ride bicycles to work.
options.B:
Riding bicycles will ensure that all of the working population of Zombieland is free
of health issues.
options.C:
The health experts suggested to the Government of Zombieland to declare riding
bicycles as mandatory.
options.D:
The Government of Zombieland believes that riding bicycles is a form of physical
exercise.

questions.explaination: The passage establishes that a complete lack of physical exercise is a primary cause of health issues, and in response, the government provides financial incentives to ride bicycles to work. This direct causal measure logically implies that the government views bicycle riding as a form of physical exercise.

questions.question_text:
Which one of the following sentence sequences creates a coherent narrative?
(i)
Once on the terrace, on her way to her small room in the corner, she
notices the man right away.
(ii)
She begins to pant by the time she has climbed all the stairs.
(iii)
Mina has bought vegetables and rice at the market, so her bags are
heavy.
(iv)
He was leaning against the parapet, watching the traffic below.
questions.explaination: Sentence (iii) introduces the protagonist Mina carrying heavy market purchases. Sentence (ii) describes the resulting exertion as she climbs the stairs. Sentence (i) brings her onto the terrace where she spots a man. Sentence (iv) details the man's posture against the parapet. Thus, the coherent sequence is (iii), (ii), (i), (iv).
questions.question_text_latex:
Which one of the following sentence sequences creates a coherent narrative?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),itemsep=0pt,topsep=2pt]
\item Once on the terrace, on her way to her small room in the corner, she notices the man right away.
\item She begins to pant by the time she has climbed all the stairs.
\item Mina has bought vegetables and rice at the market, so her bags are heavy.
\item He was leaning against the parapet, watching the traffic below.
\end{enumerate}

questions.question_text:
If ‘→’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words
[dry → arid → parched] is analogous to [diet → fast → ________ ].
Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context
questions.explaination: 'dry $\to$ arid $\to$ parched' depicts an increasing scale of lack of moisture. Similarly, 'diet $\to$ fast $\to$ starve' depicts an increasing scale of food restriction/deprivation, where starving represents extreme lack of nourishment.

Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?

blanks.
Steve was advised to keep his head (i) before heading (ii) to bat;
for, while he had a head (iii) batting, he could only do so with a cool head
s (iv) his shoulders.
questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context
questions.explaination: 'Keep one's head down' means to stay focused and avoid trouble. 'Heading out' means going forth/departing. Having a 'head for' an activity signifies natural aptitude for it, and having a cool 'head on' one's shoulders means remaining calm and composed.

questions.question_text:
If ‘→’ denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words
[walk → jog → sprint] is analogous to [bothered → ________ → daunted].
Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context
questions.explaination: 'Walk -> jog -> sprint' depicts an increasing scale of physical speed/exertion. Similarly, 'bothered -> fazed -> daunted' depicts an increasing degree of perturbation/discouragement. 'Fazed' means disconcerted or perturbed, fitting between bothered and daunted.

questions.question_text:
Sequence the following sentences in a coherent passage.
P:
This fortuitous geological event generated a colossal amount of energy and
heat that resulted in the rocks rising to an average height of 4 km across the
contact zone.
Q: Thus, the geophysicists tend to think of the Himalayas as an active geological
event rather than as a static geological feature.
R: The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice absorbed large
quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide, altering the earth’s atmosphere and
making it better suited for life.
S:
Many millennia ago, a breakaway chunk of bedrock from the Antarctic Plate
collided with the massive Eurasian Plate.
questions.explaination: Sentence S introduces the foundational historical premise (many millennia ago, Antarctic plate collided with Eurasian plate). Sentence P describes the immediate effect of this event (energy/heat rising to 4 km height). Sentence R details the subsequent cooling that altered the atmosphere. Sentence Q concludes with the geophysicists' resulting viewpoint. The logical sequence is SPRQ.
questions.question_text_latex:
Sequence the following sentences in a coherent passage.
\begin{itemize}
\item[P:] This fortuitous geological event generated a colossal amount of energy and heat that resulted in the rocks rising to an average height of 4 km across the contact zone.
\item[Q:] Thus, the geophysicists tend to think of the Himalayas as an active geological event rather than as a static geological feature.
\item[R:] The natural process of the cooling of this massive edifice absorbed large quantities of atmospheric carbon dioxide, altering the earth’s atmosphere and making it better suited for life.
\item[S:] Many millennia ago, a breakaway chunk of bedrock from the Antarctic Plate collided with the massive Eurasian Plate.
\end{itemize}

questions.question_text:
Ravi had ______ younger brother who taught at ______ university. He was widely
regarded as ______ honorable man.
Select the option with the correct sequence of articles to fill in the blanks.

options.D:
an; an; a

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.subtopic: Basic English grammar: tenses, articles, adjectives, prepositions, conjunctions, verb-noun agreement
questions.explaination: 'Younger' begins with a consonant sound (/j/), requiring the indefinite article 'a'. 'University' also begins with a consonant sound (/juː/), taking 'a'. 'Honorable' has a silent 'h' and begins with a vowel sound (/ɒ/), requiring 'an'. Hence, the sequence is a; a; an.

questions.question_text:
The CEO’s decision to downsize the workforce was considered myopic because it
sacrificed long-term stability to accommodate short-term gains.
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the word “myopic” without
changing the meaning of the sentence.
questions.subtopic: Vocabulary: words, idioms, and phrases in context
questions.explaination: 'Myopic' literally means nearsighted, and metaphorically refers to lacking foresight or being shortsighted by focusing only on immediate considerations rather than long-term outcomes.

questions.question_text:
“I put the brown paper in my pocket along with the chalks, and possibly other things.
I suppose every one must have reflected how primeval and how poetical are the
things that one carries in one’s pocket: the pocket-knife, for instance the type of all
human tools, the infant of the sword. Once I planned to write a book of poems
entirely about the things in my pocket. But I found it would be too long: and the age
of the great epics is past.”
(From G.K. Chesterton’s “A Piece of Chalk”)
Based only on the information provided in the above passage, which one of the
following statements is true?

options.A: The author of the passage carries a mirror in his pocket to reflect upon things.
options.B: The author of the passage had decided to write a poem on epics.
options.C: The pocket-knife is described as the infant of the sword.
options.D:
Epics are described as too inconvenient to write.

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee

questions.explaination: The passage explicitly states: 'the pocket-knife, for instance the type of all human tools, the infant of the sword.' Statement C directly reflects this verbatim description.
